subject: geography
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Longshore drift moves sediment along a coastline because waves approach:
options: At an angle, with swash up the beach and backwash straight down
questions.explain: The angled swash and gravity-driven backwash move material along the coast in a zigzag.

questions.q: Which is a process of coastal erosion?
questions.explain: Erosion processes include hydraulic action, abrasion, attrition and solution.

questions.q: Headlands and bays form along a coastline because:
options: Softer rock erodes faster than harder rock
questions.explain: Differential erosion of alternating hard and soft rock produces headlands and bays.

questions.q: The correct sequence of erosional landforms on a headland is:
questions.explain: Erosion of a headland progresses from crack to cave, arch, stack and finally stump.

questions.q: A spit is a depositional landform created by:
options: Longshore drift depositing material across a bay or river mouth
questions.explain: Spits form where the coast changes direction and longshore drift deposits sediment.

options: A strong backwash that removes material
A strong swash that builds beaches
questions.explain: Destructive waves have a powerful backwash and erode beaches; constructive waves build them up.

questions.q: Freeze-thaw weathering on a cliff involves:
options: Water freezing in cracks, expanding and breaking rock
questions.explain: Repeated freezing and thawing widens cracks and fragments the rock (mechanical weathering).

options: A cliff is eroded and retreats, leaving a flat rocky area at its base
questions.explain: Undercutting and cliff retreat leave a wave-cut platform exposed at low tide.

questions.q: A sea wall is an example of:
questions.explain: Hard engineering uses built structures (sea walls, groynes, rock armour) to resist the sea.

options: Trap sediment and reduce longshore drift
questions.explain: Groynes build up the beach by trapping sediment moved by longshore drift.

questions.q: Beach nourishment is a soft-engineering method that:
options: Adds sand/shingle to build up the beach
questions.explain: Nourishment replenishes beaches naturally, absorbing wave energy.

options: Allowing low-value land to flood or erode in a controlled way
Removing all people permanently by force
questions.explain: Managed retreat lets the coastline move back, often creating salt marshes that absorb energy.

questions.q: A disadvantage of hard-engineering sea walls is that they:
options: Are expensive and can look unnatural, and may increase erosion elsewhere
questions.explain: Hard defences are costly and can shift erosion problems along the coast.

options: Large boulders placed at the base of a cliff or wall to absorb wave energy
questions.explain: Rock armour dissipates wave energy and protects the coast.

questions.q: A coastal town with limited money wants a cheaper, more natural defence. A suitable option is:
questions.explain: Soft engineering is generally cheaper and more natural than hard defences.

questions.q: A stump found just offshore of a headland indicates that:
options: An arch and stack have been eroded away over time
questions.explain: A stump is the eroded remnant of a former stack, showing long-term erosion.
